The parser draws exactly the record types the table calls drawn (rich-demos-k78j.iuf)

Review of #409: the table's drawn half was read only by the staging script;
emitBlocks still decided by hand. DRAWN_RECORD_TYPES is now a typed tuple
emitBlocks dispatches over exhaustively, so a type added there does not
compile until it is drawn. dropHidden hands on RecordLines, typed records,
so the casts and the dead '?' fallback downstream go. A drawn-type record
with no message is reported malformed, not unknown. Older sessions' summary
records are hidden. The staged-types test was circular (staging filters
by the same table) and is replaced by a type on TITLE_TYPES.

Follow-up, unverified: rich-demos-k78j.5d7 (queued_command attachments).

claude-sessions opens a real session on its first message (rich-demos-k78j.iuf)

Claude Code now writes mode, attachment and a dozen other session-state
records the parser did not know, so it drew each as an "unknown record type"
error panel ahead of the conversation. Every type found across two weeks of
real transcripts is now named in RECORD_TYPES (data/parser.ts) as drawn or
hidden. A hidden record shown with H is a rule naming its type, not an error;
a type the table does not name is still drawn as an error, so it reaches the
reader.

The card's staging script took its own list of drawn types; it now derives
them from RECORD_TYPES, so the card and the Node script draw the same records.
The staged data it writes is unchanged.

Colour steps on a beat as a signal, and any effect samples on one (rich-animation-xi28.bjo)

steppedInk(steps) is an Effect whose ink steps through colours on a beat,
one a hold, looping, for the time it is handed. Each step's ink is written
as the colour nearest the step's that the depth draws and that reads on the
cell's ground at the catalogue's floor (floorOf: resting contrast or AA,
whichever is lower), measured as Effected writes it; in truecolor through
ensureContrast, the slide readableOn makes, below it the nearest indexed
colour, so at sixteen colours it steps slot to slot where the loops hold
still. The search is memoized per ink, ground and step, so a frame inside a
step redoes none.

onBeat(effect, beat) samples any effect at Beat.start(t), new on Beat: the
moment the hold in progress began, bit-identical for every t inside it. A
short-curve wheel on beat([1]) is a hue walk a step a second.

stepped <seconds> <color> ... joins frames in animationFuncs: the colour in
progress as a colour value, so it nests in fg and readableOn.

EffectCell carries reverse, so a cell and its colours make its Pair.

A transition keeps only the cells a frame lists, and a line on a blank cell shows (rich-unfiled-791c.7b9h)

/code-review medium on #408. A cell handed while blank was kept at a clamped
start and never spread over the order once it showed; it is now timed per frame
until a frame lists it. A blank cell whose style draws underline, strike,
overline, frame or encircle shows its ink, so Drawn.cells lists it.

A transition settles each cell once and spreads over the cells that show (rich-unfiled-791c.7b9h)

/code-review high on #408. A cell's change is kept from the first frame that
draws it, so an element that gains columns as it moves never sends a cell back:
renormalising every frame moved a start by up to 30% of seconds on a short
element. Drawn.cells lists only cells that show something, so padding on the
terminal's ground no longer stretches the order past the glyphs. The dissolve's
rebound weighs a cell by where it goes in the element's order. Pair has its doc
comment back, and confined reads ownership once for listed and handed cells.

A transition settles its last cell as it is done, on any element (rich-unfiled-791c.7b9h)

A transition staggered its cells by raw noise, which on a short element
spans a narrow band of the order: an 11-column dissolve settled at 21 s
and said done at 30. Drawn now lists the cells the effect will be handed
(confined narrows it to its owners'), and the order is spread over them,
so the first cell starts at 0 and the last settles at `seconds`. The
docs state the gap that is left: an ease's flat tail, and below
truecolor the last palette step.

Frames of content play on a beat for a time the host hands in (rich-animation-xi28.a3n) (#407)

* Frames of content play on a beat for a time the host hands in (rich-animation-xi28.a3n)

`beat(holds)` joins the easing vocabulary: holds in seconds, looped on
`Phase.loop`, the hold in progress out, so a sequence of unequal holds is one
beat and `steps(n)` is its equal-holds case. `Frames` draws the frame in
progress at a handed `t` — every frame at the widest one's width, ending no
line, each frame its own `RichText` — and `animationFuncs(frameTime)` registers
`frames <seconds> <frame> …` for a template, the time read when it is evaluated.

Nothing reads a clock; holds are seconds, never frame counts, and both are
tested sampled once a second and sixty times a second. A 120-column row holding
the frames renders at 0.015 ms p50 at t = 0 and at t = 10⁶ s.

* A beat lands a boundary sample on the hold that begins there, and a frame is cropped before it wraps (rich-animation-xi28.a3n)

High review on #407. beat wrapped t through (t % p + p) % p and compared
progress, so t = 0.1 on 0.1 s holds landed one ulp short and every frame
showed a sample late; now one wrapSeconds in seconds, exact at and past
zero, that Phase.loop reads too, and the one place a non-finite t fails.
Beat.holds is a copy. Frames settles its index at construction, measures
each frame once, renders without a copy, and draws noWrap + crop so a slot
narrower than the widest frame cannot fold it onto a second line. The
wall-clock p50 test is gone: the lookup it pinned is asserted by
easing.test.ts far-from-zero, deterministically.

* A negative epsilon wraps to zero, not to the period (rich-animation-xi28.a3n)

Medium review on #407: wrapSeconds carried -1e-17 up to exactly the
period, so Phase.loop answered 1 where its range is [0, 1).
